summary: Joseph Needham worked in sinology and history/archaeology. Educated at Oundle School and the University of Cambridge (Gonville and Caius College), he served as a Cambridge reader (1933–1966), Fellow of Gonville and Caius (~1924–1995), and Director of the Needham Research Institute (~1987–1990).

Joseph Prabhu works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied under Bernard Williams, Alasdair MacIntyre, and doctoral supervisor John N. Findlay. He served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007) and held several visiting professorships.

Joseph Ratzinger worked in religious studies. He studied at the University of Munich (~1947–1953) and Ducal Georgianum (1949–1951), and held posts at the universities of Munich (~1958–1959), Bonn (~1959–1963), Münster (~1963–1966), Tübingen (~1966–1969), and Regensburg (~1969–1977).

Joseph Rock worked in sinology and Tibetology. He held posts at Mills College (~1908), Mid-Pacific Institute (~1908), the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1908; 1911–1920), the United States Department of Agriculture (~1920–1924), and the Army Map Service (1944).

Joseph Tiefenthaler was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a Jesuit missionary in the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773 and held the post of Rector at the Jesuit High School of Agra.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1824, 1854, 1858) and INALCO (from 1838), and presided over the Société Asiatique.

Joseph Vendryes was a linguist who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, the Faculty of Arts of Paris, and under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the University of Paris (~1907–1946), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1907–1944), and École Normale Supérieure (~1907–1925).

Joseph Walser is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenberg, and David S. Pacini. He held a post at Loyola University Chicago (attested 1998).

Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (~1789–1799) and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1847–1849).
Josho Nozawa worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi and served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1950).
Joshu Sasaki worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Zuiryo-ji and under Joten Soko Miura, later serving as abbot at Yotoku-in (1948–1953), Shojuan (1953), and Mount Baldy Zen Center until 2012.
Joshua Ereshefsky works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He was a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2026).

Joshua Marshman worked in Indology, sinology, and linguistics. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794–1799) and under Johannes Lassar (~1805–1812), and went on to found Serampore College in 1818.

Joshua Timothy Katz is a linguist who studied at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard. He was Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022) and became a Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute (~2022).
Joshua W. C. Cutler is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (attested 2004).

Josiah Royce was a philosopher who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, Johns Hopkins University, and the University of Göttingen under Hermann Lotze. He taught at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) and served on the Harvard University faculty from 1882 to 1916.

José Ignacio Cabezón works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Caltech, Sera Monastery, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, he taught at Iliff School of Theology (~1989–2001) before becoming Dalai Lama Professor at UC Santa Barbara in 2001.
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

Jowita Kramer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Göttingen, Hamburg, and Munich. She held positions at Munich (~2005–2012, 2017–2021) and other universities, and was appointed Professor at the University of Leipzig in 2021.

Joy Brennan works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. She earned a PhD at the University of Chicago and studied under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, Constance Furey, and Diane Martin.
